label: Travelled to Europe
description: Galton's first experience of travel occurred in July 1838 when he was sixteen.

label: Travelled to Constantinople
description: Galton's first independent travel occurred when he was eighteen in 1840.

label: Set sail for Southern Africa
description: Galton set sail for Southern Africa in April 1850.

label: Wrote letter to The Times
description: In August 1851 Francis Galton wrote a letter to The Times, London from Eikhams, Namagua Land, Southern Africa.

sources.quote: In August 1851 Francis Galton (1822-1911) wrote a letter to The Times, London from Eikhams, Namagua Land, Southern Africa.

label: Published Narrative of an Explorer
description: In 1853 he wrote a book on his explorations called Narrative of an Explorer in South Africa.

sources.quote: In 1853 he wrote a book on his explorations called Narrative of an Explorer in South Africa

label: Received Gold Medal from Royal Geographical Society
description: On his return to England, he was praised for his exploration in Africa and received a Gold medal from the Geographical Society.

label: Published The Art of Travel
description: In 1855 he was encouraged to write a further book on exploration. The Art of Travel or Shifts and Contrivances Available in Wild Countries was popular

label: Published Hereditary Talent and Character
description: Galton's first published work on heredity was a two-part article in Macmillan's Magazine in 1865 called Hereditary Talent and Character.

sources.quote: Galton's first published work on heredity was a two-part article in Macmillan's Magazine in 1865 called Hereditary Talent and Character.

label: Published Hereditary Genius
description: The ideas and science in Hereditary Talent and Character were expanded in his book Hereditary Genius, published in 1869.

description: Galton first coined the term 'eugenics' in a footnote in his book Inquiries into Human Faculty and its development, published in 1883.

label: Worked alongside Joseph Jacobs
description: In 1886, Galton worked alongside Joseph Jacobs, anthropologist and historian of Jewish culture, to gather portraits of Jewish boys from a Jewish boy's school in London.

label: Published book on fingerprinting
description: In 1891, Galton published a book on fingerprinting and was responsible for proving three main characteristics of fingerprints.
